nodes.label: Todoist mapping ownership collision
nodes.norm_label: todoist mapping ownership collision
nodes.description: One remote Todoist ID must retain exactly one local owner across and within batches. The conn-level insert returns an explicit outcome (Recorded / Refreshed / RefusedOwnerConflict) instead of INSERT OR REPLACE, so a repeated claim can never silently displace the first owner.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t6-todoist-transactional-sync [ses_f20039a56ffeKhffnCGEoD418C].md:L27] "Existing RED test that must turn GREEN: services::todoist_service_tests::tests::duplicate_todoist_id_mapping_must_not_silently_displace_owner (currently second mapping silently destroys first owner via INSERT OR REPLACE on UNIQUE(todoist_id), schema.rs:262-268)" The fix is recorded at L7585: "First claim wins. The conn-level insert returns `Recorded`, `Refreshed`, or `RefusedOwnerConflict` instead of `INSERT OR REPLACE`."

nodes.label: Sync single-flight is a process static claimed before any fetch, not a UI button state
nodes.norm_label: single-flight sync job slot claimed before any fetch
nodes.description: Exactly one Todoist sync job may run per process. The slot lives in the service behind a process static claimed before any network fetch; a second invocation fails fast with a plain message. Terminal snapshots are retained until the next job begins so a remount can query them.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t6-todoist-transactional-sync [ses_f20039a56ffeKhffnCGEoD418C].md:L29] "every invocation spawns an independent job (128-160) so UI disable is not backend exclusivity" — that is the stated reason the guard had to move out of the frontend and into the backend process.

nodes.label: Absence and completion rules run only after a fetch whose stopping page carried full_sync
nodes.norm_label: absence rules gated on a complete fetch
nodes.description: sync_page_gate keeps the old stop decisions and adds a completeness flag that requires full_sync on the page where pagination stopped. Absence runs only on complete fetches with zero item failures; a partial fetch would otherwise mark every unseen local task as remotely deleted.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t6-todoist-transactional-sync [ses_f20039a56ffeKhffnCGEoD418C].md:L29] "absence/completion at 243-254 runs on whatever one fetch returned" — the defect is that one truncated page was treated as the whole remote state.

nodes.label: Each remote id reconciles in its own transaction with the mapping rechecked at mutation time
nodes.norm_label: per-item transaction rechecks mapping at mutation time
nodes.description: Create-task-plus-claim-mapping and update-owner happen atomically inside one transaction per remote id, and the mapping claim is re-evaluated at the moment of mutation rather than from the pre-fetch snapshot. Item failures are collected and fail the whole job, which skips absence rules and the last-synced update.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t6-todoist-transactional-sync [ses_f20039a56ffeKhffnCGEoD418C].md:L27] "failed mapping writes roll back" is listed as a frozen contract, and the diagnosis at L29 names the old shape: "create-then-map at 218-229 is non-transactional with ignored write errors".

nodes.label: Job correlation is added as an extra event key so existing UI readers keep working
nodes.norm_label: job id added as an extra event key not a payload change
nodes.description: todoist-sync-progress gains a job_id extra key while todoist-sync-started / -complete / -error keep their exact payload shapes; two new job-scoped events carry {job_id, ...}. todoist_get_sync_status exposes activeJob for remount recovery. No new command registration was needed.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t6-todoist-transactional-sync [ses_f20039a56ffeKhffnCGEoD418C].md:L7587] "Correlation without breaking the UI: `todoist-sync-progress` carries `job_id` (extra key, existing readers unaffected)" — the constraint was that todoist-sync-complete stays a count and todoist-sync-error stays a string because the toast reads them.

nodes.label: A rusqlite tail-expression chain keeps the MappedRows borrow alive to the end of the block
nodes.norm_label: tail expression chain extends the mappedrows borrow
nodes.description: Writing stmt.query_map(...).map_err(...)?.collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>() as one tail expression leaves the MappedRows temporary borrowed from stmt alive until the block ends, which is error[E0597]. Binding let rows = stmt.query_map(...) on its own line and collecting rows as the tail puts the drop of rows after the declaration of stmt, so it drops first. Behaviour is identical.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t6-todoist-transactional-sync [ses_f20039a56ffeKhffnCGEoD418C].md:L7625] "The tail-expression chain stmt.query_map(...).map_err()?.collect... leaves a MappedRows temporary borrowed from stmt alive until the block end. Fix by binding the rows iterator to a named local declared AFTER stmt so it drops first" — the parent's VPS compile error that produced the whole follow-up.

nodes.label: Self-deadlock from holding the global DB lock in a test
nodes.norm_label: global db lock test deadlock
nodes.description: failed_mapping_write_rolls_back_sibling_task_create hung at 0 CPU and was killed at 100s even run solo. The cause is the test holding the global DB parking_lot guard across conn.transaction() plus the create+claim calls, so something in that span re-blocks on the same non-reentrant lock. The fix was to delete the hand-rolled guard+transaction and drive the real production entry instead.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t6-todoist-transactional-sync [ses_f20039a56ffeKhffnCGEoD418C].md:L8138] "the outer `DB.lock()` guard plus hand-rolled `conn.transaction()` plus direct `create_task_and_claim_mapping_with_conn` call are replaced with `locked_test_db`, `map_local_to_todoist(\"local-owner\", \"remote-x\")`, then `crate::commands::todoist_cmds::apply_single_remote_task(&rt)`" — and the prompt at L7844 gives the reason: the test "holds the global DB parking_lot guard across conn.transaction() plus the create+claim calls, and something in that span re-blocks on the same non-reentrant lock". Reused id: chunk-rem-007 and chunk-rem-056 already carry this claim; this note adds the Todoist instance and the parked-CPU signature.

nodes.label: The claim-refusal error string is unreachable once the mapping is rechecked at mutation time
nodes.norm_label: claim refusal string unreachable through the update path
nodes.description: With only the mapping seeded, upsert_task_for_todoist_with_conn rechecks at mutation time, finds the committed owner, and takes the update path. update_task_with_conn then fails with "Task not found (local-owner)". The "already owned" string comes only from the create path's claim refusal, which cannot be reached single-threaded once the recheck sees the committed owner, so a test asserting that literal would fail deterministically.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t6-todoist-transactional-sync [ses_f20039a56ffeKhffnCGEoD418C].md:L8144] "The `\"already owned\"` string only comes from the create path's claim refusal (`create_task_and_claim_mapping_with_conn`), which is unreachable single-threaded once the recheck sees the committed owner. The specified substring would fail deterministically." Reported as a deliberate deviation from the delegation that specified the substring.

nodes.label: The day-range control is a filter, not a tab, so role=tablist is deleted rather than completed
nodes.norm_label: day-range control is not a tab so tablist is deleted
nodes.description: index.html shipped <div class="seg" role="tablist"> over three plain buttons, so a screen reader announced an empty tab list. The decision was to delete role=tablist entirely and make it a plain button group with an accessible group name plus aria-pressed on the active day, rather than add role=tab, aria-selected, tabpanel and arrow-key handling.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L44] "the day-range control is NOT a tab. It filters a range and does not swap a content panel. So DELETE `role=\"tablist\"` entirely and make it a plain button group with an accessible group name and `aria-pressed=\"true\"` on the active day. Do not half-implement the tab pattern." The defect itself is described at L35: "A screen reader announces an empty tab list."

nodes.label: A chart SVG is aria-hidden when its data is already duplicated as an adjacent list
nodes.norm_label: redundant svg hidden from at because an adjacent list already carries the data
nodes.description: #donut and #donut2 were <svg role="img"> with no accessible name while the same values were already rendered as an adjacent <ul>. Because the text equivalent exists, role="img" was removed and aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" was set instead. The 14-day #chart was deliberately not treated the same way: it has no adjacent text duplicate, so aria-hidden would be wrong there.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L37] "`#donut` and `#donut2` are `<svg role=\"img\">` with no accessible name, yet their data is already duplicated as an adjacent `<ul>`, so the svg is redundant to a screen reader." The same redundancy rule is why L47 puts aria-hidden="true" on the refresh icon: "the button already has `aria-label`, so the icon must not be announced".

nodes.label: The container name comes from aria-labelledby pointing at the visible heading
nodes.norm_label: aria-labelledby to the visible heading instead of a duplicate label
nodes.description: The heatmap wrapper got role="group" with aria-labelledby="heattitle" pointing at the section's h2, not a literal aria-label. The test resolves the name through the reference and asserts it equals the visible heading text, which is a stricter check than a bare string match.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L4121] "I gave the section heading `id=\"heattitle\"` and pointed `aria-labelledby` at it. The test resolves the name through the reference and asserts it equals the visible heading text, so this is a stricter check than a bare string match, and the visible label has one source of truth."

nodes.label: Static aria-pressed in the HTML diverges from the visual state because app.js only toggles a class
nodes.norm_label: static aria-pressed diverges from visual state after a click
nodes.description: aria-pressed="true" is now correct in the initial HTML, but main() in app.js toggles only the `on` class and never touches aria-pressed. After a click the visual state and the announced state diverge, so the day-range control announces the wrong active day. Fixing it needs one line in the click handler, which is outside this task's write scope.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L4123] "`main()` in `app.js` lines 67-74 toggles only the `on` class, never `aria-pressed`. So the correct initial value is now in the HTML, but after a click the visual state and the announced state will diverge." Reported as the one acceptance-criterion gap T3 alone cannot close.

nodes.label: A third-party webfont hands every visitor's IP address to the font host
nodes.norm_label: third-party webfont hands the visitor ip to google
nodes.description: The preconnect plus Google Fonts stylesheet for JetBrains Mono were deleted and the body stack reduced to locally available monospace faces. No @font-face, no woff2 bundling, no downloaded family name in the stack.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L4172] "Every page view makes the visitor's browser send a request to Google, so Google's infrastructure receives the visitor's IP address, tied to the fact that they opened this dashboard. The product is otherwise entirely local: local logs, a local 2B model, local CPU inference, no telemetry." The same paragraph gives the second reason: "a webfont means the dashboard silently loses its intended typeface when offline or when the font host is blocked."

nodes.label: Advance width cannot identify a monospace face; glyph ink bounding boxes can
nodes.norm_label: advance width cannot discriminate monospace faces
nodes.description: Two measurement rounds failed to identify the rendered face: total string width returned an identical value for three different families because canvas was falling back rather than resolving the names, and per-character advance returned exactly 60.00 for every monospace candidate because they all share the 0.6em advance. Switching the fingerprint to actualBoundingBoxLeft/actualBoundingBoxRight separated them and named Noto Sans Mono via the monospace generic.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L7462] "Width alone is ambiguous: three different families returned the identical 1740.00, which means canvas is not resolving those names individually." The reason advance width cannot work is at L7979: "Glyph advance widths could not distinguish the faces (all monospace faces share 0.6em advance), so the fingerprint had to be shape-based."

nodes.label: A system-installed copy of the removed webfont makes a visual check look like nothing changed
nodes.norm_label: system-installed copy of the removed font masks its removal
nodes.description: JetBrains Mono is installed as a system font on this host, so removing the webfont leaves the page looking identical and a screenshot check would have concluded nothing changed. The rendered face had to be identified by shape fingerprint to prove the webfont is gone rather than silently satisfied by a local copy.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L7979] "this host has **JetBrains Mono installed as a system font**, so a visual check alone would have been misleading. I identified the face by glyph ink bounding boxes, and `JetBrains Mono` no longer matches the rendered page while `Noto Sans Mono` and `monospace` do. That is positive proof the webfont is gone rather than silently satisfied by a local copy."

nodes.label: A clean request log means nothing until the same proxy has been seen to log an external host
nodes.norm_label: positive control through the same proxy before trusting a clean log
nodes.description: Before the real render, a request to fonts.googleapis.com was pushed through the same logging proxy to prove the detector fires. It exposed a defect in the detector itself: CONNECT lines logged 443:443 with an empty host, which would not have shown which host was contacted. Fixed, then re-run, and only then did zero LUAR lines mean zero external requests.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L7975] "I did not trust a clean log without a positive control: I first pushed `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=JetBrains+Mono` through the same proxy and confirmed it logged `CONNECT fonts.googleapis.com:443 LUAR`. That also caught a bug in my proxy, where CONNECT lines logged `443:443` with no hostname, which would not have proved *which* host was contacted."

nodes.label: A second dashboard run from the worktree overwrites a shared pid file and starts a competing tunnel
nodes.norm_label: second dashboard run competes for a shared pid file and tunnel
nodes.description: start.sh writes one shared pid file at $STATE_DIR/tli-dashboard.pid and starts a cloudflared tunnel whenever the binary and config exist. On this host cloudflared IS installed and the config exists, so a plain second run on another port would both clobber the live dashboard's pid handle and start a second tunnel on the same hostname. Isolated with TLI_STATE_DIR plus a nonexistent TLI_CLOUDFLARED_CONFIG; the shared pid file was already stale at 592337 while the live process was 489155.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L7987] "`cloudflared` **is** installed on this host, so a plain run would have started a second tunnel competing with the user's, and would have overwritten the shared pid file `~/.local/state/tli-dashboard.pid` (already stale at 592337, not 489155, before I started)." The two hazards are enumerated separately at L5521 and L5524: "Overwrite the shared pid file" and "So I must use TLI_STATE_DIR (private) and TLI_CLOUDFLARED_CONFIG (nonexistent path) to avoid both."

nodes.label: bun test on a path that does not exist exits 0, so a skip_if built on it fakes 'already done'
nodes.norm_label: bun test on a missing file exits zero fakes an idempotent skip
nodes.description: The plan's per-task idempotency guard was skip_if: "bun test ./dashboard/tests/webfont.test.ts". That command exits 0 when the file is absent — Bun prints "no matches" and exits 0 — so a dispatcher following it literally would mark the task already done and skip the work. The guard needed to fail closed on a missing file.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L7991] "`skip_if: \"bun test ./dashboard/tests/webfont.test.ts\"` exits **0** when the file does not exist (Bun prints \"no matches\" and exits 0). A dispatcher following it literally would have marked T7 as already done and skipped the task. Worth fixing in the plan for future tasks."

nodes.label: A self-referential assertion is a tautology that always fails, not a real check
nodes.norm_label: self-referential assertion is a tautology
nodes.description: expect(`${nama} ${host}`).not.toContain(`${nama} ${host}`) was written by the agent itself. A string never contains itself, so the assertion was always true and always failed. It was replaced with a real check that builds the list of (file, host) pairs where a forbidden domain appears and asserts that list is empty, which also gives a useful failure message.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L5080] "That is always true → always fails. It's a self-referential tautology (I wrote it badly). Let me fix it to be a real assertion." The same defect reappeared in the T7 webfont test and is reported at L7967: "the domain assertion was a tautology (`expect(x).not.toContain(x)`) that always failed."

nodes.label: mutation-proved test non-vacuity
nodes.norm_label: mutation-proved test non-vacuity
nodes.description: Each new test file was proved non-vacuous by mutating index.html back to the defect and confirming the matching assertion goes red, then restoring the file and verifying the restore byte-identical with diff. Seven separate mutations were caught for the ARIA contract and two for the webfont contract.
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-terminal-log-intelligence/2026-10-02 - t3-aria-contract-and-icon [ses_f05fcff42ffeEKlJqJfgHuvb4q].md:L4111] "I mutated `index.html` seven ways and restored it after each; every mutation was caught: `tablist` restored (2 fail), two `aria-pressed=\"true\"` (1), donut back to `role=\"img\"` (1), text glyph `⟳` restored (3), `?v=18` restored (1), `aria-live` removed (1), `ric-gap` class removed (1). Final restore verified byte-identical via `diff`." Reused id: chunk-rem-011 already carries this claim for app.js in the same dashboard-audit plan; this note adds the index.html instance.
